title: Relative openness of a quotient factor over an isomorphism locus
statement: Let $i:S\prime\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $J\prime\subseteq S\prime$, and $J=i(J\prime)S$. Suppose $e:S/J\cong D_1\times D_2$ is a ring isomorphism. Put $\phi=\operatorname{Spec}(i)$ and let $T$ be the image of $\operatorname{Spec}(D_1)$ under the first projection and quotient maps [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $U\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}(S\prime)$ be open and suppose the scheme morphism $\phi^{-1}(U)\to U$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism] and $T\subseteq\phi^{-1}(U)$. Then the inverse image of $\phi(T)$ in $\operatorname{Spec}(S\prime/J\prime)$ is open.

source.place: Proof of Stacks Tag 09XH, original node lines 2529-2541; verified at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09XH (image openness and final product/localization paragraphs).

proof.text: The spectrum image of the first projection from a product is D((1,0)). The kernel consists of elements (0,b), so a prime contains that kernel iff it omits (1,0): one direction uses (0,1)+(1,0)=1, the other uses (a,b)(1,0)=0. Transport through e. The quotient spectrum embedding then gives T=V(J) intersect D(t) for any lift t of e^{-1}(1,0).

The restricted scheme isomorphism gives an open immersion into Spec(S prime) after composing with the inclusion of U. Apply its open-map property to the inverse image of D(t) to see W=phi(D(t) intersect phi^{-1}(U)) is open.

A prime q contains map i J prime iff its inverse image contains J prime. Thus phi^{-1}(V(J prime))=V(J). Using T subset phi^{-1}(U), obtain phi(T)=W intersect V(J prime). Pullback by the quotient map has inverse image of V(J prime) equal to the whole spectrum and is continuous, so the desired inverse image is open.
